title: Trump makes extraordinary promise to give EVERY American adult $5,000
text:
By VICTORIA CHURCHILL, US POLITICAL REPORTER and ASSOCIATED PRESS

Published:  11:16 AEST, 10 September 2026   |  Updated:  00:50 AEST, 11 September 2026

4.9k

View  comments

President Donald Trump promised to give every American adult a $5,000 'dividend' if Republicans hold both chambers of Congress in November.

He made the pledge at the Republican Midterm Convention in Dallas on Wednesday evening.

'If the Republicans win, you win with us, and you get $5,000,' Trump stated on stage as more than 21,000 attendees looked on. 'It will be called the Trump Dividend.'

He likened the payments to a corporation's distributions to shareholders, citing 'our tremendous strength and success economically.'

The proposal, which would cost $1 trillion, reflects Trump's bold strategy to boost Republican chances, as Democrats look to capitalize on his low approval ratings.

The president said the only caveat would be that recipients spend the money in the United States.

Commenting on how the party performs worse when his name is not on the ballot, Trump also urged Republicans to treat November's midterms as a referendum on himself, telling the party's first ever midterm convention: 'I'm asking you to pretend I'm on the ballot.'

The plea, delivered on the opening night of the two-day gathering, demonstrated how the GOP's fate remains tethered to a president who will not face voters himself as it fights to hold Congress.

Trump opened his remarks by reviving his false claim that he won the 2020 election, declaring: 'We won the presidency three times.' He lost to Joe Biden in 2020.

US President Donald Trump shakes hands with attendees as he arrives to speak during the Republican National Midterm Convention at the American Airlines Center in Dallas

People pause during the program on the first day of the 2026 Republican National Convention

He then gave the Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, the struggling GOP nominee for the state's US Senate seat in a razor-thin race with Democrat James Talarico, a Trumpian-endorsement.

'He may not dress right. He may not talk exactly perfectly, and he may not be the best-looking guy I've ever seen. But you know what he is? He's the greatest attorney general in America, and he deserves to be your next senator,' Trump said.

Later, Trump described the Democrats as pushing 'bulls***,' noting they have more of it 'than any human beings on the planet' as he commented on the Democrats opposing federal photo ID mandates when voting.

The president walked out to Lee Greenwood performing God Bless The USA, and the contrast with prior speakers was stark.

The crowd had sat through the earlier slate of speakers showing little energy, but then hung on Trump's every word. Trump is scheduled to speak on both nights of the convention.

Still, the weeks' guest list tells its own story about Trump's cratering popularity.

Senate Majority Leader John Thune is not speaking, a snub that follows Trump's frustration with the South Dakotan over stalled pieces of his agenda, even as other House and Senate leaders were handed slots.

Several candidates in the country's most competitive races are also skipping the main stage, among them Maine's Republican Senator Susan Collins, Congresswoman Ashley Hinson who is running for the US Senate in Iowa, and John E Sununu, the Republican nominee trying to flip New Hampshire's Senate seat red.

Most experts predict Democrats will win back the US House of Representatives, but the Senate will be tougher to flip with battleground races in Maine, Ohio, Michigan and Alaska set to determine control.

Trump's own trip to Texas was delayed Wednesday after his new Qatari-gifted Air Force One deployed its emergency evacuation slide.

And his keynote had competition too, with the NFL season kicking off the same night with the New England Patriots at the Seattle Seahawks, a rematch of February's Super Bowl.

More than 20,000 convention attendees descended to take part in the historic midterm gathering. But not all of the party faithful were excited about the event.

One GOP lobbyist told Politico Playbook: 'the vibes are very bad,' while two others remarked that Trump will be competing for attention with the start of the NFL season.

Some seats were empty at the opening of the first day of the Midterm Republican National Convention as crowds waited outside in 95 degree heat

US Air Force personnel remove an emergency inflatable slide after it deployed on Air Force One before President Donald Trump arrived to board it on his way to Dallas

Republican National Committee Chairman Joe Gruters holds up a giant gavel as he speaks

House lawmakers including Anna Paulina Luna of Florida and Derrick Van Orden of Wisconsin were early speakers on Wednesday's slate.

Luna attacked Democrats for their history of self-serving stock trading, and Van Orden boosted Trump's Rural Healthcare plan.

US Senate nominees including Ken Paxton of Texas, Michael Whatley of North Carolina, and Mike Collins of Georgia are expected to speak, as is incumbent Ohio Senator Jon Husted.

Trump's cabinet secretaries including Brooke Rollins, Scott Bessent, Dr Mehmet Oz, and even Attorney General Todd Blanche are on the agenda as well.

The two-day event will also include a tribute to conservative activist Charlie Kirk, who was assassinated while speaking on the campus of Utah Valley University last September. Trump paid homage to Kirk, and his wife Erika during his remarks on Wednesday, calling his murder a 'shock,' as well as the people who 'made an excuse for it or cheered for it.'

The 25th anniversary of 9/11, taking place on Friday, will also be commemorated during Thursday's programming at the convention.
